item.title: Waldschmidt constants and invariant geometry for exceptional rank-four complex reflection groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.13108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the Waldschmidt constants of the point configurations dual to the reflection arrangements of the exceptional complex reflection groups $G_{29}$, $G_{31}$ and $G_{32}$. They equal $3$ for the forty points of $G_{29}$, $36/11$ for the sixty-point Klein configuration, and $10/3$ for the forty-point Penrose configuration. Together with the known cases $W(F_4)$ and $W(H_4)$, this completes the computation for all exceptional irreducible complex reflection groups of rank four. An invariant dodecic and its sixfold orbit product give extremal surfaces for the first two configurations, and we identify the six dodecics as pullbacks of the coordinate hyperplane sections of the Segre cubic under the Igusa-Segre duality. The matching lower bounds follow from restriction to quadrics and distinguished planes, including a weighted B\'ezout estimate arising from two related Hesse arrangements. As a consequence, we determine the asymptotic resurgences of the three ideals.
item.dc:creator: Krishna Hanumanthu, Jack Huizenga, Jake Kettinger, Lukasz Merta, Tomasz Szemberg, Justyna Szpond

item.title: Reciprocal mirror map derivatives, euler-twisted Gromov-Witten invariants, and instanton counts via quantum Serre duality
item.description: arXiv:2611.13126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study mirror map derivatives as a means of relating the genus zero Gromov-Witten theories of an anticanonical Calabi-Yau hypersurface in a smooth, almost minimal Fano variety and the local Calabi-Yau formed from the total space of the Fano's canonical bundle with the euler-twisted theory of the ambient Fano. A precise relationship between reciprocal mirror map derivatives is obtained from the non-equivariant limit of quantum Serre duality for the euler-twisted theory of the ambient Fano as formulated by Iritani, Mann, & Mignon. This allows us to express the generating series of 3-point euler-twisted invariants as the derivative of the local mirror map with respect to the closed one. In low dimensions, this series is shown to be a modular form of Eisenstein type which has arisen before in this area. We prove integrality of the twisted invariants from this identification. The regularized small quantum $D$-module of the Fano is reducible, and we show it is equivalent to an inhomogeneous Picard-Fuchs equation governed by this generating series. The reciprocal mirror map derivative is then shown to be a generating function of local 3-point invariants, which recovers some known results for local Calabi-Yau threefolds and proves a conjecture of the second named author and A. Malmendier in previous work on local fourfolds. Explicit calculations for $\mathbb{P}^2,\mathbb{P}^3$ and $\mathbb{P}^4$ illustrate these relationships, which includes the vanishing of positive-degree ordinary genus-zero invariants for anticanonical elliptic curves and K3 surfaces, the recovery of the quintic threefold's instanton numbers, and finally some formulas for genus-zero invariants of local projective spaces.
item.dc:creator: Irit Huq-Kuruvilla, Michael T. Schultz

item.title: The Cayley-Bedregal reduction for Milnor and Hirzebruch-Milnor classes
item.description: arXiv:2611.13267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Cayley--Bedregal reduction replaces a complete intersection $\{f_1=\dots=f_r=0\}$ by the hypersurface $\sum_i\varphi_if_i=0$ in the projectivized dual bundle. For an isolated complete intersection singularity of corank $c$, we express the Milnor class of this hypersurface on its singular fibre $\mathbb P^{c-1}$ in terms of the Milnor numbers of generic systems obtained by taking linear combinations of the defining equations. Its degree is the original Milnor number, and the higher components recover the Milnor numbers of the systems with fewer equations. These numbers are invariants of the analytic germ. Our second main result concerns the Hodge-theoretic refinement. For a complete intersection defined by a regular section of a rank-$r$ algebraic vector bundle, the Hirzebruch--Milnor class is determined by that of the Cayley--Bedregal hypersurface: the push-forward of the normalized Hirzebruch--Milnor class of the hypersurface, in the sense of Cappell, Maxim, Sch\"urmann and Shaneson, is $(-y)^{r-1}$ times that of the complete intersection, with no positivity assumption on the bundle. The factor $(-y)^{r-1}$ comes from the motivic decomposition of the projective bundle, and at $y=-1$ the identity recovers Aluffi's comparison of Milnor classes. When the tautological bundle is very ample, the hypersurface formula of Maxim, Saito and Sch\"urmann then gives the Hirzebruch--Milnor class of the complete intersection through the vanishing cycles of a single function, avoiding their induction through intermediate complete intersections and their restriction to powers of one line bundle. In integral homology we prove the analytic form of Aluffi's identity, and obtain formulas for the Milnor class in terms of local Milnor fibres and for the Chern--Schwartz--MacPherson class of any projective scheme.
item.dc:creator: R. Callejas-Bedregal, F. Caraballo, M. F. Z. Morgado, J. Seade

item.title: On Poincar\'e-Type Inequalities for Flags of Distributions
item.description: arXiv:2611.13349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish enumerative formulas and derive geometric inequalities for flags of holomorphic distributions on complex manifolds. First, given a codimension-one holomorphic distribution $\mathcal{G}$ on a complex manifold $M$, we establish an upper bound for the number of independent holomorphic $p$-distributions tangent to $\mathcal{G}$ with a prescribed associated twisting line bundle $\mathcal{L}$. As an application, we prove Poincar\'e-type degree inequalities for flags on certain classes of manifolds. Finally, we investigate the Mumford--Takemoto stability of the tangent sheaves of rank-two distributions. In particular, we establish several stability results for such distributions on projective spaces, smooth weighted complete intersection threefolds, and, in particular, on smooth hypersurfaces $V\subset\mathbb{P}^4$.
item.dc:creator: Antonio M. Ferreira, Miguel Rodr\'iguez Pe\~na, Fernando Louren\c{c}o

item.title: Unimodal Singularities of Parametrized Space Curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.13377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aim of the article is to classify unimodal parametrized space curve singularities defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$. We provide explicit normal forms of parametrizations up to $\mathcal A$-equivalence. The parametrizations are given by convergent power series over a real valued field, which includes parametrizations given by formal power series and by, for example, convergent power series over the complex numbers or the field of Puisieux series. The list of normal forms is surprisingly simple.
item.dc:creator: Gert-Martin Greuel, Khawar Mehmood, Gerhard Pfister

item.title: $5I(K_X+\Delta)$ is very ample on stable log surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.13381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that Bombieri's bound for canonical models of surfaces of general type extends to stable log surfaces, that is, $mI(K_X+\Delta)$ is very ample for every $m\geq 5$ and every stable log surface $(X,\Delta)$ over $\mathbb{C}$ with reduced boundary and global Cartier index $I$. On the way to this result we determine the cases where $|3I(K_X+\Delta)|$ has base points.
item.dc:creator: Wenfei Liu, S\"onke Rollenske

item.title: Gromov-Witten Nonvanishing and Symplectic Deformations of Toric Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.13422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A$ be nonzero in the cohomology ring of a smooth projective toric variety $X$. In this note, we observe the existence of a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant of the form $\langle A, A, \ldots\rangle_{0, n,\beta}^X$ as a consequence of Iritani's work on the big quantum cohomology ring of $X$. This implies Koll\'ar's conjecture on the symplectic deformation invariance of rational connectedness in the case where $X$ is toric. If $X$ is moreover Fano and $B$ is also nonzero in the cohomology ring, we prove the existence of a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant of the form $\langle A,B,*\rangle_{0,3,\beta}^X$ using Batyrev's presentation of the small quantum cohomology ring of $X$. We conclude with a few consequences of this nonvanishing result.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Tausik

item.title: A cyclotomic Artin-Tate formula and sphere packing for K3 surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.13468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give new necessary conditions on the Weil polynomial of a K3 surface over a finite field using techniques from the theory of sphere packing. By comparing the Artin-Tate formula over a finite extension, we derive a special values formula at roots of unity that involves the discriminant of the Frobenius coinvariant lattice. Known bounds on the minimum discriminants of even rootless lattices then imply nontrivial lower bounds on these special values. Applying these new conditions to Kedlaya and Sutherland's list of candidate Weil polynomials of K3 surfaces over the field with 2 elements rules out over 50% of the candidates.
item.dc:creator: Asher Auel, Sair Shaikh

item.title: Essential $p$-dimension of simple algebras and noncrossed products of prime exponent
item.description: arXiv:2611.13747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and $F$ a field of characteristic different from $p$. For integers $n\ge2$ and $1\le m\le n$, we complete the determination of the essential $p$-dimension of the class of central simple algebras of degree $p^n$ and exponent dividing $p^m$. In particular, we have $\operatorname{ed}_p(\operatorname{PGL}(p^n))=p^{2n-2}+1$, extending a result of Merkurjev for $n=2$. Using the comparison theorem of Chernousov and Merkurjev, we also determine the essential $p$-dimension of every split simple group of type $A$. To obtain the lower bounds, we apply a theorem of Ofek to block centralizers. As an application, we prove the existence of division algebras of exponent $p$ over field extensions of $F$ which remain noncrossed products after any field extension of degree prime to $p$, and answer in the negative a problem in the survey by Auel, Brussel, Garibaldi, and Vishne. The algebras can be chosen to have degree $p^n$ for every $n\ge3$ if $p$ is odd and every $n\ge4$ if $p=2$. For $p=2$ and every $n\ge3$, we also determine the essential $2$-dimensions of the classes of central simple algebras of degree $2^n$ with orthogonal involution and with symplectic involution.
item.dc:creator: Sanghoon Baek

item.title: Non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory and stacks
item.description: arXiv:2611.13877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the first half of these notes, we survey some aspects of the stack-theoretic perspective on $p$-adic Hodge theory, with an emphasis on the non-abelian aspects. In the second half, we report ongoing joint work on ``quantizing'' non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory.
item.dc:creator: Bhargav Bhatt

item.title: On Algebraic LNE models of complex affine algebraic curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.14071v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a sufficient condition for an affine complex curve to have an algebraic complex LNE model.
item.dc:creator: Zbigniew Jelonek, Karolina Zaj\k{a}c

item.title: Loops and mirrors
item.description: arXiv:2611.14110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a smooth affine complex variety X we construct a Q-algebra LH(X), loop cohomology, in terms of the formal-loop space of X. We conjecture that it is isomorphic to the symplectic cohomology of X. The degree-zero loop cohomology subalgebra is finitely generated for polarized log Calabi-Yau X, constructing an intrinsic mirror affine coordinate ring. Its polyvector algebra is identified with the full loop cohomology algebra for a positive log Calabi-Yau pair with maximal boundary and smooth loop mirror, proving a form of mirror symmetry. In this case we further identify the degree-zero loop cohomology algebra with the Gross-Siebert intrinsic mirror algebra. Assuming in addition that X is a surface, we prove that the full loop and symplectic cohomology algebras agree.
item.dc:creator: Nero Budur

item.title: Affine Springer fibers, Cherednik algebra modules and Hilbert schemes: torus link case
item.description: arXiv:2611.14190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a pair of positive integers $M,N$ with GCD $d$, we relate the bigraded $S_N\times S_d$-Frobenius characters of the homology of the positive part of a homogeneous affine Springer fiber for $\mathrm{GL}_N$ of slope $M/N$ to a direct sum of the associated graded of minimal supported modules of type $A_{N-1}$ rational Cherednik algebra at the same slope, and to the equivariant K-theory of a coherent sheaf on the Hilbert scheme of points on the plane. For the first object, we use the Hessenberg paving of Goresky-Kottwitz-Macpherson; for the second and third objects, we resort to an explicit Hodge module on $\mathfrak{sl}_N$. The bridge between them is a non-coprime shuffle theorem of Kim-Oh.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Boixeda Alvarez, Thomas Hameister, Xinchun Ma

item.title: Virtual Two-Step Nilpotency of the Fundamental Groups of Special Quasi-Projective Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.14283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the fundamental group of every smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety that is special in the sense of Campana is virtually nilpotent of class at most two. This establishes the two-step nilpotency conjecture of Cao--Deng--Hacon--P\u{a}un, a quasi-projective analogue of Campana's almost abelian conjecture for special compact K\"ahler manifolds. Examples of Cadorel--Deng--Yamanoi show that the step bound is sharp. On a suitable finite etale cover, we construct a canonical second Albanese map to a torus torsor over an abelian variety. The proof reduces to showing that the kernel of the induced map on fundamental groups is finite. Using good minimal models and meridian groups of projective pairs, we show that an infinite kernel would yield a saturated rank-one subsheaf of logarithmic differentials whose Iitaka dimension contradicts specialness.
item.dc:creator: Tianshu Jiang, Jiayu Li

item.title: Irrationality and Noether--Lefschetz loci in the moduli space of K3 surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.14294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The goal of this paper is twofold. First, we construct examples of families of surfaces where the locus of points in the base with constant degree of irrationality is not constructible. Second, we explore the notion of gonality loci in the moduli space of K3 surfaces, which are characterized by the existence of a smooth curve with fixed gonality. Among various results, we prove that polarized gonality loci are always unions of Noether--Lefschetz divisors.
item.dc:creator: Dori Bejleri, Nathan Chen, Benjamin Church, Kristin DeVleming

item.title: Ramification of torsion packets on curves with good-reduction Jacobians
item.description: arXiv:2611.14337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p\ge5$ be a prime number, $k$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. Write $R=W(k)$ for the ring of Witt vectors over $k$, and $K$ for the field of fractions of $R$. Let $X$ be a smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve over $K$ of genus greater than one. Write $J$ for the Jacobian variety of $X$. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{K}$ of $K$. In the present paper, we prove that if $J$ has good reduction over $R$, then every point $x\in X(\overline{K})$ such that $[\sigma x-x]$ is torsion for each $\sigma\in \operatorname{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)$ is $K$-rational.
item.dc:creator: Arata Minamide

item.title: On the topology of some linear systems of hyperelliptic curves in Hirzebruch surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.14386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Following a program suggested by Dolgachev and Libgober in 1981, we study the topology of the locus of smooth sections of linear systems of hyperelliptic curves on Hirzebruch surfaces. Our primary interest is the computation of various flavors of ``enriched monodromy representations''. Within this class of examples, we find that a variety of behaviors occur - in some situations the enriched monodromy faithfully captures the fundamental group, and in others it does not. Our arguments mainly leverage algebro-geometric techniques to compute cohomological obstructions to families of embeddings.
item.dc:creator: Nick Salter

item.title: Canonical Volumes of Threefolds with Positive Geometric Genus
item.description: arXiv:2611.14402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a complex projective threefold of general type with canonical singularities and positive geometric genus has canonical volume at least $1/30$, with strict inequality when its Euler characteristic is positive. We describe the equality cases as canonical hypersurfaces of degree $28$ in $\mathbb P(1,3,4,5,14)$. These canonical models and their smooth projective resolutions are simply connected. Their coarse moduli space is irreducible and rational of dimension $103$, with finite quotient singularities; all admissible $\mathbb Q$-Gorenstein deformations are unobstructed and arise by varying the equation.
item.dc:creator: Pinxian Bie, Peien Du, Zhengjie Yu

item.title: On the stable birational type of Fano threefolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.14417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that, given a very general cubic threefold $X$, any smooth cubic threefold stably birational to $X$ must be isomorphic to $X$. The method applies as well to other Fano 3-folds, like the sextic double solid, and the quartic threefold. We also discuss the higher-dimensional case.
item.dc:creator: Claire Voisin

item.title: Shifted Lagrangian structures and syzygies on Calabi--Yau varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.14453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In \cite{FMR25}, Fantechi--Mir\'o-Roig show how to construct new Lagrangian subspaces of the moduli of simple perfect sheaves on a K3 surface from a given one. We reinterpret their construction using the tools and flexibility of derived algebraic geometry. This allows us to generalize from K3 surfaces to (possibly singular) Calabi--Yau schemes of arbitrary dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Enrico Lampetti, Luca Morstabilini

item.title: Koszul duality and determinant formulas for affine hyperplane arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2611.13050v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For real affine hyperplane arrangements, we prove Lam's determinant conjecture for the inverse Varchenko matrix restricted to bounded chambers. The proof combines Lam's comparison of twisted intersection forms with the period determinant formula of Varchenko, Loeser-Sabbah and Douai-Terao. For normal crossing arrangements, we introduce the taut path algebra and the chamber intersection algebra and establish a Koszul duality between them, yielding an explicit multivariate formula for the inverse Varchenko matrix. After specializing the parameters to $q$, its restriction to bounded chambers is a scalar multiple of the $q$-intersection matrix, proving a determinant conjecture of the authors. We also discuss how the Koszul duality results generalize to affine oriented matroids.
item.dc:creator: Jens Niklas Eberhardt, Carl Mautner

item.title: The $\mathbb Q$-gonality of $X_1(42)$ is $12$
item.description: arXiv:2611.13155v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the $\mathbb F_5$-gonality and the $\mathbb Q$-gonality of the modular curve $X_1(42)$ are both $12$, improving the previous lower bound of $10$. Since $J_1(42)(\mathbb Q)$ is finite, it follows that $12$ is the least degree in which $X_1(42)$ has infinitely many points. The lower bound comes from an exhaustive search over Riemann--Roch spaces, following Derickx and van Hoeij, using a new reduction by the orbits of a cyclic group of automorphisms of order $12$ on places of degree at most $5$ ($743\,231$ Riemann--Roch spaces). An earlier search with the reductions from van Hoeij's code (about $3$ million Riemann--Roch spaces, about $6$ times more CPU time) gives the same result and serves as supporting evidence. We prove the reductions and record the data needed to reproduce the computations.
item.dc:creator: Sourajyoti Maiti

item.title: A decomposition theorem for minimal W-algebras of type A
item.description: arXiv:2611.13239v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: To any simple Lie algebra, one can associate a minimal affine W-algebra. It is a vertex algebra which is obtained from the universal affine vertex algebra by a chiral Hamiltonian reduction procedure. This reduction is determined by data coming from the minimal nilpotent orbit. It is a chiral quantisation of the Slodowy slice associated to this minimal orbit. In this paper, when the simple Lie algebra is of type A, we prove that the minimal W-algebra is isomorphic to a commutant subalgebra in a localisation of the universal affine vertex algebra. Then, we establish a decomposition theorem \`a la Losev: the localised universal affine vertex algebra decomposes as the tensor product of the minimal affine W-algebra and another vertex subalgebra. As a direct corollary, we retrieve the celebrated result of inverse Hamiltonian reduction for the minimal W-algebra. We also prove an analogue of this result for the corresponding finite W-algebra. In both cases, our approach relies on the geometry of the associated Slodowy slice.
item.dc:creator: Thibault Juillard

item.title: On the number of zeros of polyanalytic polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.13278v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a complex polynomial $f(z,\bar z)$ of degree $n$ in $z$ and degree $m<n$ in $\bar{z}$, with finitely many zeros, has at most $(4m+1)n-5m$ distinct zeros in $\mathbb{C}$. The proof uses an approach suggested by GPT-6.1 based on a topological result of Kronheimer and Mrowka (Thom's Conjecture). We provide examples showing that the bound is asymptotically sharp as $n\to\infty$ for each fixed $m$.
item.dc:creator: Erik Lundberg, Zvi Rosen, Teng Zhang

item.title: Closed layers in tensor-triangular geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.13284v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the absence of a theory of closed immersions in tensor-triangular geometry, we propose an alternative approach via quotients of module categories. As an application, we prove invariance of homological residue fields under completion.
item.dc:creator: Paul Balmer, Rhea Kommerell, Emmy Van Rooy

item.title: Uniform symmetric spectral finiteness of semialgebraic cones
item.description: arXiv:2611.13376v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cone-constrained eigenvalues of a matrix are defined through a complementarity problem constrained by a closed convex cone. We show that every closed semialgebraic convex cone is uniformly symmetrically spectrally finite; that is, the cone spectra, the sets of the cone-constrained eigenvalues, of symmetric matrices relative to the cone are uniformly finite with respect to the matrices. The uniform bound is explicit, and as an application, we derive a uniform bound for the cardinality of spectra of symmetric matrices relative to L\"{o}wner cones. In addition, using the uniform finiteness of cone spectra, we also show the uniform finiteness of the number of singular values relative to two closed semialgebraic convex cones. For non-semialgebraic cones, we observe two contrasting phenomena. On the one hand, we show that the exponential cone is uniformly symmetrically spectrally finite. On the other hand, we provide a closed non-semialgebraic convex cone such that the associated cone spectra of symmetric matrices are finite but are not uniformly finite.
item.dc:creator: Mitsuhiro Nishijima

item.title: Cluster-theoretic Newton--Okounkov polytopes of flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.13385v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Newton--Okounkov bodies have been used for studying toric degenerations of flag varieties. We classify the Newton--Okounkov polytopes associated with cluster valuations and the anticanonical line bundle on full flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$. In type $A_4$, the $672$ seeds of cluster type $D_6$ yield $162$ affine unimodular equivalence classes, which coincide with the combinatorial equivalence classes. We determine the subgroup of exchange-graph automorphisms preserving every polytope class. It is a Klein four group of index six in the automorphism group of the exchange graph of cluster type $D_6$. In type $B_2$, we give defining inequalities for all six seeds. At the anticanonical weight, the two combinatorial equivalence classes split into three affine unimodular equivalence classes. Their respective class-preserving automorphism groups have orders four and two.
item.dc:creator: Shin Hong, Jeongsoo Kim, Eunjeong Lee

item.title: Differential Monodromy, $q$-Opers, and Universal $(G,q)$-Wronskians
item.description: arXiv:2611.13446v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a geometric formulation of the $q$DE/ODE/IM correspondence for families of differential operators associated with simple Lie algebras of ADE type. Under analytic hypotheses, the $q$-connection associated with shifted monodromy defines a twisted $(G,q)$-oper and has Steinberg form in the frame of solutions normalized by prescribed asymptotics in a sector at infinity. We identify the central connection between the normalized solution frames at zero and infinity with a universal meromorphic $(G,q)$-Wronskian. Its generalized minors give $Q$-functions satisfying the ADE $QQ$-relations. When $q$ is not a root of unity, we parametrize shifted monodromy by quantum-affine $q$-characters evaluated on shifted $Q$-ratios, using the same character formulas that describe normalized transfer-matrix eigenvalues. We verify the analytic hypotheses for generic untwisted Feigin--Frenkel--Hernandez affine opers, thereby relating these affine opers to twisted $(G,q)$-opers.
item.dc:creator: Anton M. Zeitlin

item.title: Regular loci of affine Springer fibers at very special parahoric level
item.description: arXiv:2611.13601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For split groups, we prove that centralizers act transitively on regular loci of affine Springer fibers at very special parahoric level. As an application, we prove Chi's conjecture on the number of top-dimensional irreducible components of affine Lusztig varieties.
item.dc:creator: Ryosuke Shimada

item.title: Periods and CM motives of abelian type
item.description: arXiv:2611.13723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We associate algebraic Hecke characters to certain invertible motives for absolute Hodge cycles with coefficients in a number field $K$, reversing a viewpoint of Schappacher. These motives $N$ include abelian motives and a new notion of algebraic motive. This Hecke character determines the complex and the $p$-adic periods of $N$, and is determined by the latter; this gives a proof of the Mumford-Tate conjecture for $N$. When $K$ and $N$ are abelian, we prove a refinement of the Gross-Deligne conjecture, as well as $l$-adic and $p$-adic variants. We also formulate a version of the algebraic relations between rational values of the gamma function given by Koblitz and Ogus in terms of a distribution with values in the Picard group of the category of (abelian) Chow motives.
item.dc:creator: Bruno Kahn, Noriyuki Otsubo

item.title: Rank Additivity and Comon's Conjecture for Real Hankel Tensors
item.description: arXiv:2611.13823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathscr{H}_m(n)$ denote the set of real Hankel tensors of order $m$ and dimension $n$, and let $\textbf{H}\in\mathscr{H}_m(n)$, where $m\ge3$ and $n\ge1$. Set $M=(m-1)(n-1)+1$. First, we prove that the CP rank $r(\textbf{H})\le M$ and that CP rank is additive under direct sums of $\textbf{H}$ with any real tensor $\textbf{T}$ of the same order. Second, we prove that partially symmetric rank $p_j(\textbf{H})=r(\textbf{H})$ for $1\le j\le m-1$ and that, if $r(\textbf{H})\le M-1$, these ranks also equal its symmetric rank $s(\textbf{H})$. Third, we construct a fourth-order Hankel tensor $\textbf{H}_*\in\mathscr{H}_4(4)$ that attains this CP rank bound and satisfies $r(\textbf{H}_*)=10$ and $s(\textbf{H}_*)=11$. Moreover, for the direct sum $\textbf{H}_*^{(k)}=\bigoplus_{a=1}^k\textbf{H}_*$, we further prove that $r(\textbf{H}_*^{(k)})=10k$ and $s(\textbf{H}_*^{(k)})=11k$. This provides a low-dimensional counterexample to Comon's conjecture over the real numbers and further shows that the Comon rank gap is unbounded among real symmetric tensors of order four.
item.dc:creator: Jianze Li

item.title: Singular points of envelopes and offsets: a transition from 2D to 3D
item.description: arXiv:2611.14005v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We recall properties of the offsets of a (plane) kiss curve and their singularities, then we make a transition to 3D, considering the surface obtained by revolution of the kiss curve about one of its axes. When pos?sible, geometric constructions using automated methods are performed. This induces a need to focus on algebraic computations. Networking be?tween different kinds of software is of utmost importance, in order to use their respective strengths (dynamic geometry, dragging points, strong al?gebraic computations, etc.). A core difference between the 2D and 3D situations is that automated commands existing in 2D are not available in 3D. This makes the DGS less relevant in 3D than in 2D. In 3D, most of the work must be performed with the CAS. The singular points of a kiss curve in the plane are tacnodes (cusps) and crunodes (self-intersection). The singularities are not isolated anymore and cuspidal edges appear. In this setting, implicitization is a heavy endeavour and we need another technology, related to AI; we describe this briefly. The 2D activities have been proposed to in-service teachers learning towards an advanced degree.
item.dc:creator: Thierry Dana-Picard, Arie Haenel, Daniel Tsirkin

item.title: Hamiltonian GKM spaces via Gromov-Witten theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.14020v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use equivariant Gromov-Witten theory to prove the generalised symplectic Mukai inequality for Hamiltonian GKM spaces with large pseudoindex or a special vertex, including smooth Schubert varieties. We also classify all Hamiltonian GKM graphs when the pseudoindex is at least the complex dimension, obtaining a Hamiltonian GKM analogue of the classical Kobayashi-Ochiai classification of complex projective space and complex quadrics. Of independent interest are our connectivity theorem for a low-magnitude subgraph of the GKM graph (reminiscent of Campana and Koll\'ar-Miyaoka-Mori's rational chain connectedness of Fano manifolds), and a local Mukai-type theorem that applies at each vertex. We obtain corollaries on reflexive Delzant polytopes that are purely combinatorial in nature.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Holmes

item.title: Asymptotically good codes from Siegel modular varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.14125v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct asymptotically good codes by evaluating Siegel modular forms at superspecial points on congruence towers of Siegel modular varieties. For every genus $g\ge2$ and every fixed weight $w\ge g+1$, the construction gives such a family in sufficiently large characteristic, over a finite field which is independent of the level of the tower. The towers can be chosen so that this field is $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$. We give an explicit lower bound for the asymptotic rate. The lower bound for the relative minimum distance follows from the Pieri formula on the space of flags in the Hodge bundle and an intersection argument along its strata. We also prove that, for $p\ge5$ and $0\le w\le p+1$, the kernel of evaluation in every genus consists precisely of the multiples of the ordinary Hasse invariant. For $g=2,3$, the geometry of the supersingular locus gives explicit bounds for the relative minimum distance and recovery sets whose sizes are bounded independently of the level.
item.dc:creator: Yota Maeda

item.title: Non-closed products in branch and weakly branch groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.14127v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the first Grigorchuk group and the Gupta-Sidki $3$-group are not double coset separable, disproving a conjecture of Grigorchuk, Leemann and Nagnibeda. More generally, every finitely generated regular branch group with bounded activity contains two finitely generated, profinitely closed subgroups with trivial intersection whose product is not closed. Every infinite finitely generated subgroup of the first Grigorchuk group or the Gupta-Sidki $3$-group also fails to be double coset separable. We extend the construction to the $p$-Basilica groups and, using polynomial activity, to the long-range group, whose derived subgroup we prove to be finitely generated. Under an additional hypothesis on finite quotients, we determine the closure of the product. Membership in the constructed product is decidable in the first Grigorchuk group.
item.dc:creator: Daniele D'Angeli, Emanuele Rodaro

item.title: The elliptic Hall algebra and the combinatorics of affine Springer fibers
item.description: arXiv:2611.14177v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For coprime positive integers $m,n$ and $k\ge1$, we study the symmetric functions $e_k[-X^{m,n}Y]\cdot1$ arising from the elliptic Hall algebra action. We identify their $\omega_X$-transforms with the normalized bigraded Frobenius characteristics computed by Boixeda Alvarez--Hameister--Ma for the torus-equivariant Borel--Moore homology of the positive parts of homogeneous affine Springer fibers. We introduce cyclic LLT polynomials and determine their monomial expansions, yielding explicit monomial formulas for these elliptic Hall algebra expressions in terms of cyclic parking functions. These results extend the affine Springer fiber identity and monomial formula of Carlsson--Mellit from integral slopes to arbitrary positive rational slopes.
item.dc:creator: Donghyun Kim, Jaeseong Oh

item.title: A Complete Classification of Maximal Hyperelliptic Curves Related to Chebyshev Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.14198v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\varphi_d$ be the Chebyshev polynomial with $\varphi_d(t+t^{-1})=t^d+t^{-d}$, and let $H_d$ be the hyperelliptic curve $y^2=\varphi_d(x)$. We determine all pairs $(d,p)$, with $p\nmid2d$ prime, for which $H_d$ is maximal over some finite field of characteristic $p$, together with all such fields. For $p\equiv1\pmod4$ only partial results were known. In this case, for odd $d$ we show that the Jacobian of $H_d$ is supersingular if and only if $H_d$ is maximal over a finite extension of $\mathbb{F}_p$, and that this happens precisely when $d=\ell^n$ with $\ell\equiv1\pmod4$ prime and $p$ a generator of $(\mathbb{Z}/\ell^n\mathbb{Z})^\times$; we also compute the Frobenius polynomial. Necessity comes from the Shimura--Taniyama formula together with the non-vanishing of the value at $0$ of certain Dirichlet L-series and information about the action of Frobenius on $2$-torsion. The case of even $d$ and $p\equiv1\pmod 4$ follows from the odd case, by a short reduction.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Tafazolian, Jaap Top

item.title: Splitting module-finite extensions over singular local rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.14347v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study when a module-finite extension of a singular local ring splits as a module over the base. On a Gorenstein curve of positive residue characteristic, weak normality forces splitting for every extension of finite projective dimension. In residue characteristic two the converse holds when two is zero or a nonzerodivisor. A missing square root in the prescribed base gives an explicit nonsplit extension of generic rank four. We obtain a second curve criterion by gluing retractions on the branches and determine all evaluation ideals for coordinate crossings and for \(x^2=y^2u z_1\cdots z_s\) in odd characteristic. For cubic extensions we prove a presentation theorem with arbitrarily many relations. It applies on the blow-up of an ideal generated by a regular sequence of length three, and on the blow-up of a three-dimensional local ring with a quadric tangent cone. A family of matrices satisfying the criterion exists over every residue field in the regular-sequence case.
item.dc:creator: J. D. V\'elez

item.title: On the symplectic cohomology of orbifold divisor complements
item.description: arXiv:2611.14449v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This article studies the symplectic cohomology of Liouville domains whose contact boundaries admit a periodic Reeb flow, with a particular focus on affine varieties which arise as orbifold divisor complements. We describe a computation of the transverse Conley-Zehnder indices which allows for a simple computation of the positive equivariant symplectic cohomology in cases when the inertia orbifold of the compactifying divisor has only even cohomology. This is then applied to the classification of orbifold compactifications of $\mathbb{C}^n$. Moreover, we study the action of multiplication by the principal orbit on V-shaped symplectic cohomology and prove that if the compactification $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{D})$ is positively monotone, then this class induces a periodic structure on symplectic cohomology, reducing the problem of computing an infinite-dimensional group to a finite-dimensional repeating portion. We combine the index computations and this periodic structure to compute the symplectic cohomology of various Milnor fibers of surface singularities, the rational homology balls $B_{p,1}$ as well as complements of star-shaped configurations of rational curves in K3 surfaces, which includes the Milnor fibers of the exceptional unimodal singularities.
item.dc:creator: Bogdan Simeonov, Elliot Gathercole

item.title: Newton non-degenerate holomorphic foliations and their separatrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.14466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we study germs of holomorphic foliations in the complex plane that are Newton non-degenerate. This is an algebraic condition attached to the Newton polygon of the foliation, analogous to the one defined by Kouchnirenko for analytic curves and, more generally, hypersurfaces. As in this case, the condition of Newton non-degeneracy for foliations can be identified through the comparison of two numerical invariants: the Newton number - a computation involving simple geometric data of the Newton polygon - and the Milnor number. The Newton number is never greater than the Milnor number, and the foliation is Newton non-degenerate if and only if they are equal. The assumption that a foliation is Newton non-degenerate imposes conditions on its set of separatrices. We prove that, under this hypothesis, the foliation has no weak separatrices and, hence, all its separatrices are analytic. We also give a description of the set of separatrices of a Newton non-degenerate foliation, which is sufficient to characterize the foliation as Newton non-degenerate when it is of generalized curve type. This allows us to prove that the property of being Newton non-degenerate is topologically invariant for foliations of generalized curve type.
item.dc:creator: Arturo Fern\'andez-P\'erez, Evelia R. Garc\'{i}a Barroso, Rog\'erio Mol

item.title: Classifiyng metrically conical rational singularities
item.description: arXiv:1112.0125v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We will in this article classify which rational complex surface singularities are metrically conical, that is have the bilipschitz type of their inner metric equivalent to that of a cone. This is done using the thick-thin decomposition for the inner geometry of a normal complex surface singularity and properties of rational singularities. The result is a family of singularities depending only on their topology which is given as a $3$-parameter family.
item.dc:creator: Helge M{\o}ller Pedersen

item.title: Monodromy and vanishing cycles for complete intersection curves
item.description: arXiv:2408.06479v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the topological monodromy of every family of complete intersection curves. Like in the case of plane curves previously treated by the second-named author, we find the answer is given by the $r$-spin mapping class group associated to the maximal root of the adjoint line bundle. Our main innovation is a suite of tools for studying the monodromy of sections of a tensor product of very ample line bundles in terms of the monodromy of sections of the factors, allowing for an induction on (multi-)degree.
item.dc:creator: Ishan Banerjee, Nick Salter

item.title: Projective Variety Recovery from Unknown Linear Projections
item.description: arXiv:2504.16771v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how a smooth irreducible variety $X$ of dimension $n$ and degree $d$ in $\mathbb{P}^m$, $m\geq n+2$, can be recovered from the equations of its images under two generic projections from unknown centers. This extends earlier results on curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ and surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^4$ to any dimension. Since $X$ is the normalization of each image, one image determines $X$ modulo the projective group when $X$ is linearly normal; what two images add is the configuration, that is the pair of projections. For complete intersections we prove unconditionally that the set of configurations compatible with the two images and their Hilbert polynomial is finite, of size at most $|\mathrm{Lin}(X)|$, the projective automorphism group of $X$. The argument is effective and the bound is attained. We then introduce an equation generalizing Kruppa's equation, relating the duals of the images to a fundamental matrix, encoding the pair of projections modulo the projective group. We give a necessary condition for its solution variety to be finite, a bound on its isolated points, and a sufficient condition under which the true fundamental matrix is rigid: no quadric may contain a generic line $L$ together with the locus of points of $X$ whose tangent space meets $L$. Rigidity is unconditional for curves; in higher dimension it holds under a first-order liftability hypothesis, which we certify for a del Pezzo quartic surface in $\mathbb{P}^4$. Global finiteness of that solution variety remains open, necessarily so, as it contains solutions realized by no variety; for $\dim X<\mathrm{codim}\,X-1$ the obstruction amounts to knowing the fundamental matrix itself. Once the projections are known, $X$ is recovered from the two cones over the images: in codimension two their intersection is $X$ plus a component of degree $d(d-1)$; in higher codimension $X$ is its unique component of maximal dimension.
item.dc:creator: Yirmeyahy Kaminski

item.title: On the volume of K-semistable Fano manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2506.17420v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the anti-canonical volume of an $n$-dimensional K-semistable Fano manifold that is not $\mathbb{P}^n$ is at most $2n^n$. Moreover, the volume is equal to $2n^n$ if and only if $X\cong \mathbb{P}^1\times \mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ or $X$ is a smooth quadric hypersurface $Q\subset \mathbb{P}^{n+1}$. Our proof is based on a new connection between K-semistability and minimal rational curves.
item.dc:creator: Chi Li, Minghao Miao

item.title: Arcs on rational double points in arbitrary characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2508.12423v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We settle the Nash problem for two-dimensional rational double points in all characteristics. The proof is based on a direct computation of the families of arcs through these singularities.
item.dc:creator: Tommaso de Fernex, Shih-Hsin Wang

item.title: Computing weighted sheaf cohomology using noncommutative differential modules
item.description: arXiv:2510.02131v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe a novel method for computing sheaf cohomology over weighted projective spaces and stacks using exterior algebra and differential module techniques, generalizing an algorithm due to Eisenbud-Fl{\o}ystad-Schreyer over projective space.
item.dc:creator: Michael K. Brown, Daniel Erman

item.title: Stacky geometry and logarithmic topology of transversely affine foliations
item.description: arXiv:2605.27669v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the linear monodromy of codimension-one transversely affine foliations through multiplicative quotient stacks and logarithmic boundary topology. When the transverse affine structure admits a global presentation on $U$, a choice of multiplicative developing coordinate induces a morphism to $[\mathbb{C}^*/\Gamma]$, where $\Gamma\subset\mathbb{C}^*$ is the image of the linear monodromy. We prove that for infinite $\Gamma$ every strict semi-equivariant holomorphic self-map of $\mathbb{C}^*$ is a monomial, and classify the nonconstant strict semi-equivariant rational self-maps of $\mathbb{P}^1$ for arbitrary $\Gamma$. For a logarithmic connection along a simple normal crossings divisor, we describe the meridional characters and angular foliations on the boundary fibres of the Kato--Nakayama space, including the topology and closures of their leaves. We also describe the extension of the linear monodromy local system to this space and the effect of local Kummer base change on finite meridional monodromy.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Barbassa, Gabriel Santos Barbosa, Maur\'icio Corr\^ea

item.title: Mirror symmetry for gCICY threefolds (I): a $[3,-1]$ block and a non-Gorenstein toric phase
item.description: arXiv:2610.03719v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct and analyze a mirror family for the generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau threefold $X_+=[\mathbb{P}^1\,|\,3\ {-1};\ \mathbb{P}^4\,|\,2\ 3]$, with $(h^{1,1},h^{2,1})=(2,46)$. We introduce auxiliary variables to obtain a toric GIT presentation with two chambers. The first gives $X_+$, while the second gives a Calabi-Yau threefold $X_-$ related to $X_+$ by a flop of 16 disjoint $(-1,-1)$-curves. The threefold $X_-$ is a nef complete intersection in a non-Gorenstein toric $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano eightfold. Then the Hori-Vafa equations give a 2-parameter Laurent family, and we construct a smooth projective crepant model $Y$ of its general member with mirrored Hodge numbers. The rank-6 Picard-Fuchs system of $Y$ has two maximally unipotent boundary points, whose indicial algebras are isomorphic to the even cohomology rings $H^{\mathrm{even}}(X_+,\mathbb{C})$ and $H^{\mathrm{even}}(X_-,\mathbb{C})$. We also show that the predicted genus-zero BPS numbers of the first two vertical degrees agree with direct counts of lines and conics on the genus-one fibration $X_-\to\mathbb{P}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Atsushi Kanazawa

item.title: The commuting scheme of $\mathfrak{g}_2$ and a degree formula for commuting schemes
item.description: arXiv:2610.05018v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Over a field of characteristic zero, we show that the commuting scheme of the exceptional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}_2$ is Cohen-Macaulay and normal (in particular, reduced). We determine its Hilbert series, show that it has degree $1825$ and is not Gorenstein, and determine an explicit linear system of parameters. A crucial ingredient of (one of) our proofs is a root theoretic formula for the degree of the commuting scheme of any reductive Lie algebra whose Borel subalgebra has a complete-intersection commuting scheme, which includes all classical Lie algebras of small rank as well as $E_6$ and $G_2$. Finally, we give a criterion that implies Cohen-Macaulayness and reducedness of the commuting scheme in any given positive characteristic and use it to show that the commuting scheme is Cohen-Macaulay and reduced for every prime $5\leq p\leq1000$. We also resolve the `bad' characteristic cases and show that the commuting scheme is reduced and Cohen-Macaulay over fields of characteristic $3$, and reduced but not Cohen-Macaulay over fields of characteristic $2$ where it has degree $438$.
item.dc:creator: Pallav Goyal

item.title: Special Loci in the Moduli of Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.08382v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce new techniques to study mixed-characteristic special loci in moduli spaces and give several applications, focusing in particular on the moduli space $\mathsf{M}_g$ of curves. These applications include Zariski density results for split Jacobians, non-density results for supersingular loci, and lifting results for algebraic cycles, all under appropriate numerical conditions. Our methods generalize to more-or-less arbitrary moduli spaces mapping to Hodge-type Shimura varieties (and even some settings beyond the Shimura case), and relate to questions raised by Oort and de Jong.
item.dc:creator: David Urbanik, Ziquan Yang

item.title: Stable compatibility for model categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.00813v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By introducing the notion of stable compatibility, we provide a framework in the model category theory which addresses the existence of a stable model structure on the category of modules over a monad. Exact version of such monads have been studied in the setting of triangulated categories, separately as separable monads a la Balmer in tensor triangular geometry and non-separable monads a la Dell'Ambrogio and Sanders in stable homotopy theory. By introducing stable compatibility, we explore their properties together and produce a non-separable monad in Algebraic geometry and more.
item.dc:creator: Kunal Arora, Vivek Mohan Mallick

item.title: Fujita's Very Ampleness Conjecture for $\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$-Bundles over Curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.09532v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a vector bundle of rank $n\geq 2$ over a smooth projective curve $C$ over $\mathbb{C}$. We prove that $\omega_{\mathbb{P}_C(\mathcal{E})}\otimes\mathcal{L}_1\otimes\dots\otimes\mathcal{L}_k$ is very ample for arbitrary ample line bundles $\mathcal{L}_i$ on ${\mathbb{P}_C(\mathcal{E})}$ when $k\geq n+2$.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Dao

item.title: $2$-adic integral models of some Shimura varieties with parahoric level structure
item.description: arXiv:2301.12981v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct integral models over $p=2$ for some Shimura varieties of abelian type with parahoric level structure, extending the previous work of Kim-Madapusi, Kisin, Pappas, and Zhou. These integral models are canonical in the sense of Pappas-Rapoport.
item.dc:creator: Jie Yang

item.title: The Bruce-Roberts Tjurina number of holomorphic 1-forms along complex analytic varieties
item.description: arXiv:2409.19814v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the notion of the \textit{Bruce-Roberts Tjurina number} for holomorphic 1-forms with respect to a pair $(X,V)$ of complex analytic subvarieties. We characterize its finiteness and, when $X$ and $V$ are hypersurfaces with at most isolated singularities, relate it to a determinantal colength, the Tjurina number of the 1-form with respect to $V$, and the Tjurina number of $X$. We also establish a decomposition of the difference between the Bruce-Roberts Milnor and Tjurina numbers and a bound for their quotient. As an application, we prove a relative quasihomogeneity result for germs of non-dicritical generalized curve foliations in complex dimension two.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Barbosa, Arturo Fern\'andez-P\'erez, V\'ictor Le\'on

item.title: A conditional proof of the Casas-Alvero conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2501.09272v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Casas-Alvero conjecture states that if $f(X)$ is a monic univariate polynomial of degree $d$ over a characteristic $0$ field $\mathbb{K}$ such that $\gcd(f, f_{i})$ is non-trivial for each $i=1, \dots, d-1$, then $f(X)=(X-\alpha)^d$ for some $\alpha\in \mathbb{K}$. In this paper, we prove the Casas-Alvero conjecture for polynomials of any degree $d\geq 3$ over any characteristic $0$ field, under a uniform local {\L}ojasiewicz type hypothesis for a family of polynomials obtained from the elementary symmetric functions. Furthermore, we prove this estimate on compact subsets of a common Zariski open set of coefficients parametrizing the family.
item.dc:creator: Soham Ghosh

item.title: Pellarin's Identity, Carlitz Period, and Anderson Generating Functions over Arbitrary Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.03134v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish three results for a rank-one Drinfeld module over the coefficient ring of a smooth, projective, geometrically connected curve over $ \mathbb F_q$, with a closed point at infinity of arbitrary degree. First, a Tate-algebra unit exists in the module of special functions precisely when this module is free of rank one, that is, when the period lattice is isomorphic to the module of regular differentials; this proves the Gazda--Maurischat conjecture. Second, under the unit-anchor normalization for an isogeny to a principal-period target, a strictly normalized shtuka product and one characteristic residue give the fundamental period; the same defect equation gives the logarithm residue formula. Third, finite \'{e}tale torsion traces over the field of definition identify the first Frobenius twist of the normalized shtuka differential and express Pellarin's $ \mathcal L(1)$-series at a fundamental period. The source period lattice need not be free.
item.dc:creator: Chuangqiang Hu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Lishan Yu

item.title: Local Tate duality for syntomic cohomology in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.21622v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $k$ be a local field of characteristic $p>0$. We show that syntomic cohomology over $k$, with coefficients, and defined using Dodd's theory of $F$-gauges, satisfies local Tate duality. We also prove that syntomic cohomology over the ring of integers of $k$, again with coefficients, is Lagrangian with respect to the duality pairing. Finally, we show that, for $p>2$, these results recover Shatz's duality and Milne's orthogonality results for the cohomology of finite flat group schemes of $p$-power order over $k$.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Lazda

item.title: The Kemper--Malle conjecture and isolated linear quotient singularities
item.description: arXiv:2610.29849v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the Kemper--Malle conjecture, which provides a modular analogue of the Chevalley--Shephard--Todd theorem. As a consequence, the classification of isolated linear quotient singularities over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic reduces to the classical Zassenhaus--Vincent--Wolf classification.
item.dc:creator: Yang Chen

item.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35492v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove an expansion in $1/g$ of the Weil--Petersson volumes $V_{g,n}$ that is uniform over all cusp counts, from fixed $n$ to arbitrarily large $n/g$. An explicit leading term and single-factorial remainder bounds give exponentially small relative errors after truncation at a suitable order proportional to $g$. A positive recursion along the string flow connects these volumes to pure $\psi$-class intersection numbers, where Painlev\'e~I fixes the normalization; uniform coefficient extraction then recovers individual volumes. We determine Zograf's constant $C=1/\sqrt\pi$ and resolve Mirzakhani's two questions on volume ratios for growing cusp counts and adjacent coefficient ratios uniformly over all degrees. Via Mirzakhani's integration formula, the same volume estimates control random surfaces at two distinct scales. At $n/\sqrt g\to c\in(0,\infty)$, the entire positive Laplace spectrum below $1/4$ converges to an explicit Poisson point process generated by geodesics cutting off two cusps. Together with Huang's theorem, this characterizes the transition for $n\ge1$: the spectral gap tends in probability to $1/4$ exactly when $n/\sqrt g\to0$, and to $0$ exactly when $n/\sqrt g\to\infty$. At density $n/g\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, we identify the local limit around a typical point; its cusp-filling is conformally a disc. As $\lambda\to\infty$, these limits approach the infinite Weil--Petersson sphere of Budd and Curien. We prove their parabolicity conjecture and, by a growing-radius coupling, answer their scaling-limit question: after deep cusps are trimmed, the rescaled infinite sphere converges to the Brownian plane.
item.dc:creator: Qihang Wang, Zhiyi Li, Bolin Qiu, Shuaijia Wang, Yuan Zhong, Kun Chen, Renqiu Xia

item.title: Symplectic Cuts and Moment Polyptychs of Hypertoric Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.37724v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study compact symplectic cuts of hypertoric varieties and characterise their smoothness. When the defining arrangement has a non-empty bounded base region, the fibre-rotation action has a proper moment map and gives compact K\"ahler orbifold cuts at regular levels. For a smooth hypertoric manifold, an outer-chamber cut, taken above the largest critical value of this moment map, is smooth if and only if the manifold is the cotangent bundle of its distinguished compact toric subvariety; that subvariety is then a product of projective spaces, and every positive level is regular with a smooth cut. If the compact core of a smooth hypertoric manifold is reducible, every outer-chamber cut has a boundary point with non-trivial cyclic isotropy and a singular coarse local quotient, whereas every cut below the smallest positive critical value is smooth. We introduce the moment polyptych, assembled from truncated arrangement regions, and recover the residual fixed points, tangent weights, and finite local groups from its edges and labelled lattice data. Restriction to arrangement flats is compatible with cutting and supplies the lower-dimensional models used in these calculations. The resulting local data are applied to equivariant quantisation in a companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin C. W. Brown
